issues.legal_issue: A ceiling on agricultural land held for personal cultivation applies whenever a person holds land exceeding the permissible limit, not only to holdings exceeding the limit when the ceiling regime commenced.
material_facts: The landowner owned agricultural land exceeding the applicable ceiling but was dispossessed by trespassers when the earlier law required landowners to select land for personal cultivation.
The landowner was restored to possession after the ceiling provisions had taken effect.
The land was declared to exceed the applicable ceiling, and the landowner challenged that determination.
issues.conclusion: The ceiling applies whenever a person is found to own or hold land under personal cultivation exceeding the permissible limit; its operation is not confined to the commencement date.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32-A(1) imposes a continuing restriction in its plain terms. Sections 32-L and 32-M address particular subsequent acquisitions but do not restrict the general operation of section 32-A(1). The scheme of Chapters II, III and IV, as originally enacted, allowed selection of land for personal cultivation and tenant purchase of unselected land; Chapter IV-A changed that scheme by imposing a ceiling and providing for surplus land to be appropriated to the State. Section 32-B provides machinery for holdings existing at commencement but does not limit section 32-A to that date. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.ceiling_landholding_proceeding: The proceeding determines whether a person's agricultural landholding exceeds an applicable ceiling.
predicates.personal_cultivation_exceeds_limit: A person owns or holds agricultural land under personal cultivation in an aggregate area above the applicable permissible limit.

issues.definition: When a proceeding concerns a landholding above the applicable limit for personal cultivation, the ceiling restriction applies.

issues.legal_issue: A landowner who could not meet the deadline for undertaking and planting an orchard because the land was not in their possession during the planting period cannot obtain an orchard exemption by having the deadline extended judicially.
material_facts: The landowner was dispossessed before the ceiling provisions commenced and was not restored to possession until after the two-year period for planting an orchard had expired.
The landowner sought to reserve additional land for an orchard under the exemption.
The landowner could not give and fulfill the required undertaking within the specified period, and the legislation provided no extension for this exceptional situation.
issues.conclusion: The landowner could not claim the additional area for an orchard; the Court could not extend the planting period, and any remedy for the legislative omission lay with the legislature.
issues.legal_principle: Section 32-K(1)(vi) required a written undertaking to plant an orchard within two years of commencement of the amending law. Section 32-K(2) provided for the land to vest in the State if the orchard was not planted within that period, and section 32-K(3) required the land to remain an orchard when exemption was granted. The Court could not read the specified period as running from the date possession was restored or otherwise supply an extension omitted by the legislature. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: orchard_exemption_claim and land_recovered_after_planting_deadline and orchard_not_planted_within_deadline and no_special_extension_provided

predicates.orchard_exemption_claim: A landowner seeks to retain land on the basis that it will be used to establish an orchard.
predicates.land_recovered_after_planting_deadline: The landowner regained possession only after the period available for establishing the orchard had expired.
predicates.orchard_not_planted_within_deadline: The landowner did not establish the orchard within the applicable planting period.
predicates.no_special_extension_provided: The governing scheme provides no extension of the planting period for a landowner in these circumstances.

issues.definition: An orchard exemption is unavailable when a landowner seeks it, regains possession after the planting period, has not planted the orchard within that period, and no special extension is provided.
